title: Deep Blue defeats Garry Kasparov in their 1997 rematch
summary: IBM's Deep Blue defeated reigning World Chess Champion Garry Kasparov in their six-game rematch, winning the match 3.5-2.5 after Game 6 on May 11, 1997.
significance: A documented AI and high-performance-computing milestone in which a computer system defeated a reigning world chess champion in a match under standard tournament controls.

geography.note: IBM's historical account places the May 1997 rematch at the Equitable Center in New York. This geography describes the documented match location, not Deep Blue's development ancestry or organizational origin.

verification.note: IBM's official history records the May 1997 New York rematch, Deep Blue's 3.5-2.5 victory, and its status as the first computer system to defeat a reigning world chess champion in a match under standard tournament time controls. IBM's 2001 annual-report historical caption identifies May 11, 1997 for the Kasparov-versus-Deep-Blue event, supporting day precision for the victory milestone. No ancestry, influence, causality, or development geography is inferred.

candidateMeta.admissionReason: IBM primary sources support the documented 1997 victory milestone, exact date, match result, and match-location geography. The candidate keeps those facts separate from unsupported ancestry, development geography, influence, or causality.
